title: Prophet Muhammad (570-632)
notes: Cited for: Mount Hira and the 610 command to recite (the traditional story); revelations continued and became the Quran; message of no god but God and submission; Meccan elite saw him as a threat; hijra of 622 begins the Islamic calendar.

title: The Qur'an
notes: Cited for: revealed in Arabic over 23 years; suras not in chronological order; text established under the caliph Uthman (Muslim belief); Muslims taught to recite in Arabic; hafiz; hadith chains of narration.

title: Basic articles of faith
notes: Cited for: the six articles of faith; prophets from Adam to Jesus with Muhammad the final prophet; God has no children, parents or partners; predestination alongside free choice; Muslims worship only God.

title: Five Pillars of Islam
notes: Cited for: the five pillars listed; they give a Muslim's life its framework; faith without practice regarded as pointless.

title: Shahadah: the statement of faith
notes: Cited for: the wording of the shahada; sincere recitation is all a person needs to become a Muslim.

title: Zakat: charity
notes: Cited for: 2.5% of wealth each year for the poor; zakat as worship and self-purification; wealth as on loan from God.

title: Salat: daily prayers
notes: Cited for: the five prayer times; wudu and mosque washing facilities; no priest as intermediary, the imam is not a priest; praying anywhere, and together as equals.

title: Sawm: fasting
notes: Cited for: reasons for the fast (self-discipline, sympathy for the poor); avoiding evil thoughts and deeds; suhur and breaking the fast with dates.

title: Eid al-Fitr
notes: Cited for: Eid al-Fitr thanks God for strength to practise self-control during Ramadan; a time of forgiveness and making amends.

title: Hajj: pilgrimage to Mecca
notes: Cited for: simple white ihram clothing strips away markers of status so all are equal; Hagar's search for water between Safa and Marwa and the Zamzam spring (Muslim belief); Arafat, Muzdalifa and the stoning at Mina.

title: Sunni and Shi'a
notes: Cited for: the larger group chose Abu Bakr as caliph; a smaller group held that Ali should lead; meanings of Sunni and Shi'a; both share the Quran and the fundamentals and agree Muhammad was the final prophet.

title: Sharia
notes: Cited for: qiyas example (drugs ruled forbidden by analogy with alcohol, both intoxicating).

title: Khadijah
notes: Cited for: a merchant who employed Muhammad to manage a caravan to Syria; often considered the first person to believe his message; reassured him about his first revelations.

title: Islam
notes: Cited for: islam literally 'surrender', a Muslim accepts surrender to the will of God; Muhammad the last of a series of prophets including Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Solomon and Jesus.

title: Muhammad (collected reference entries, incl. International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences)
notes: Cited for: in the Quran Muhammad is presented as a human being with no divine qualities; in Islamic tradition a messenger of God and the 'seal of the prophets'.

title: Qur'an (Encyclopedia of Islam and the Muslim World, via Encyclopedia.com)
notes: Cited for: the refined art of Quran recitation shown at popular competitions where renowned reciters, both male and female, display their skills.

title: Tawhid
notes: Cited for: tawhid, 'making one' or 'asserting oneness', God as a unity not made up of parts; expressed in the shahada.

title: Allah
notes: Cited for: Allah as the standard Arabic word for God, used by Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews; probably from al-Ilah, 'the God'; shirk as the one sin God will not forgive in the hereafter.

title: The World's Muslims: Unity and Diversity, Chapter 3: Articles of Faith
notes: Cited for: core articles of faith (one God, prophets, scriptures, unseen angels, Day of Judgment, predestination with free will); belief in one God and Muhammad nearly unanimous in most of 39 countries; belief in fate from under half in Albania to over nine in ten in Azerbaijan and Turkey.

title: Pillars of Islam
notes: Cited for: the five pillars; shahada wording; zakat of one-fortieth of cash and savings beyond a minimal threshold; hajj at least once in a lifetime barring physical or financial hardship.

title: Salat
notes: Cited for: the five prayers (fajr, zuhr, asr, maghrib, isha); facing the Kaaba in parallel rows; Friday congregational prayer with two sermons instead of the prayer just after noon.

title: Islam: Prayer
notes: Cited for: ablutions of hands, face and feet; each unit with standing, a genuflection and two prostrations, 'God is great' at every change of posture; the muezzin's call from a raised place; prayers may be offered individually.

title: Great Mosque of Mecca
notes: Cited for: the Kaaba, 'cube', a cube-shaped shrine near the center of the Great Mosque; the qibla for the five daily prayers; pilgrims walk around it counterclockwise seven times.

title: Ramadan
notes: Cited for: ninth month; fasting dawn to dusk; exemptions; revelation believed to have begun on one of the last 10 nights in 610; suhur and iftar with dates; Quran 2:183; false words as destructive of a fast as eating; Eid al-Fitr customs.

title: Eid al-Adha
notes: Cited for: 'Festival of Sacrifice', one of Islam's two major festivals; begins 10 Dhu al-Hijjah at the culmination of the hajj; commemorates Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son Ishmael, replaced by a ram; meat divided among the poor, relatives, friends and household.

title: Hajj
notes: Cited for: 7th to 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah; once in a lifetime if physically and financially able; ihram garments (two white seamless sheets for men, women may wear sewn clothes); seven circuits of the Kaaba; seven times between Safa and Marwah; stones at Mina; sacrifice; hair shaved or a lock cut.

title: Shi'i
notes: Cited for: Ali, cousin and son-in-law, as rightful successor in Shi'i belief; Ali the fourth caliph, killed in 661; Husayn killed at Karbala in October 680, mourned at Ashura; Twelvers and the hidden twelfth Imam.

title: Sunni
notes: Cited for: Sunnis recognize the first four caliphs as Muhammad's rightful successors; four orthodox schools of law (Hanafi, Hanbali, Maliki, Shafii).

title: Mapping the Global Muslim Population
notes: Cited for: Sunni and Shia identities formed around a succession dispute after Muhammad's death in 632; 87-90% Sunni and 10-13% Shia; Shia majorities in Iran, Azerbaijan, Bahrain and Iraq.

title: Hadith
notes: Cited for: hadith as sayings and traditions of Muhammad, second only to the Quran for law, ritual and creed; sunnah; isnad and matn; sahih, hasan, daif; al-Bukhari (d. 870) and Muslim (d. 875); Shi'i collections incl. al-Kulayni's Kitab al-kafi.

title: Aishah
notes: Cited for: after Muhammad's death Aisha spent her years transmitting hadith and interpreting the Quran; described as issuing legal opinions.

title: Fiqh
notes: Cited for: sharia considered divine and immutable; fiqh, the human effort to know it, imperfect and changeable.

title: Sharia: Development of different schools of law
notes: Cited for: Malikis and Hanafis gave more weight to regional traditions, al-Shafii to Quran, Sunnah and analogy; where each school came to predominate; 'Difference of opinion among my community is a sign of God's bounty.'
